Verratti shares this record with his teammate Marquinhos, who also has nine titles. Paris Saint-Germain has been very successful in Ligue 1, contributing to these players’ impressive achievements in the league

1. Marco Verratti (9 titles)
Marco Verratti, the Italian midfielder, is the record-holder for the most Ligue 1 titles, having won nine with Paris Saint-Germain (PSG). Verratti joined PSG in 2012 from the Italian club Pescara. In his first season, he became a key player in PSG’s midfield.
He helped PSG win the Ligue 1 titles in 2013–14, 2014–15, and 2015–16. The 2019–20 season was particularly remarkable for Verratti and PSG. The team won a domestic treble, winning the Ligue 1 title, Coupe de France, and Coupe de la Ligue.
Verratti’s impressive performances led to a contract extension, keeping him with PSG until June 2024. In the 2020–21 season, Verratti reached his 300th appearance for PSG in a Ligue 1 match against Monaco.
He also set a record for the most Champions League appearances for the club, with 58. The 2021–22 season was another milestone for Verratti. PSG won Ligue 1 for the tenth time. Verratti won his eighth Ligue 1 title that season, becoming the first player to achieve this feat.
In the 2022–23 season, Verratti won his ninth Ligue 1 title with PSG, breaking his record. This achievement confirmed his status as one of the greatest players in PSG’s history and one of the most successful players in Ligue 1.
Verratti’s influence at PSG went beyond individual awards. He was crucial in the team’s success, controlling the game, making key passes, and defending effectively.
In September 2023, Verratti left PSG after 11 years and 416 matches, making him the second-most capped player at the club. He signed a three-year contract with Al-Arabi in Qatar for a transfer fee of €45 million.
2. Marquinhos (9 titles)
One of the players who have won the most Ligue 1 titles is Marquinhos, the Brazilian center-back. He has made a significant mark in the history of Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) by winning a record-breaking nine Ligue 1 titles with the club.
Born in São Paulo, Brazil, Marquinhos started his professional career with Corinthians in 2012. After a brief loan to Roma, he joined PSG in 2013 for a fee of €31.4 million. This transfer was one of the highest ever for a player under 20 years old.
Since arriving in Paris, Marquinhos has been a key part of PSG’s defense. He has played alongside great players like Thiago Silva and Presnel Kimpembe, forming strong partnerships that have helped the team succeed.
His strong performances have earned him a place in the Ligue 1 Team of the Year several times. After Thiago Silva left in 2020, Marquinhos took over as the captain of the team. Marquinhos’ achievements with PSG are impressive.
He has been part of the team that won nine Ligue 1 titles, which is a record for the club. Also, he has won 13 domestic cups, proving he can perform at the highest level consistently. Marquinhos is also known for having the most appearances in PSG’s history.
Internationally, Marquinhos made his debut for the Brazilian national team in 2013 and has played in two FIFA World Cups (2018 and 2022) and three Copa Américas (2019, 2021, and 2024), winning the title in 2019. His performances with Brazil have further established him as one of the best defenders in the world.

3. Presnel Kimpembe (8 titles)
Presnel Kimpembe is a professional footballer born on August 13, 1995, in Beaumont-sur-Oise, France. He plays as a center-back for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and the France national team.
Kimpembe has won an impressive eight Ligue 1 titles with PSG, making him one of the most successful players in the league’s history. Kimpembe started his football career in the youth ranks of AS Éragny.
In 2005, he joined PSG’s academy, where he began to develop his skills. He made his professional debut for PSG on October 17, 2014, in a match against Lens.
Over time, he grew into a key player for PSG, known for his strong defensive abilities and good game understanding. One of Kimpembe’s best moments was in the UEFA Champions League.
He made his debut in this competition on February 14, 2017, helping PSG keep a clean sheet against Barcelona. In February 2019, Kimpembe scored his first goal for PSG in a Champions League match against Manchester United.
Throughout his career with PSG, he has been a crucial part of their success, helping the team win many league titles. Kimpembe has also played for France at various levels, including the senior team. He was a member of the squad that won the 2018 FIFA World Cup.
Despite facing challenges, such as a serious Achilles tendon injury in February 2023, Kimpembe has shown determination to return to the field. PSG recognized his value and renewed his contract until 2026.
4. Kylian Mbappé (7 titles)
Kylian Mbappé, who is currently playing for Real Madrid is one of the best football players in the world today. He was born on December 20, 1998, in Paris, France, and began his professional career at AS Monaco.
In the 2016-17 season, he helped AS Monaco win the Ligue 1 title, scoring 15 goals. In 2017, Mbappé moved to Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) for a big fee. At PSG, he has continued to impress and win titles.
As of the end of the 2023 season, he has won a total of seven Ligue 1 titles: one with AS Monaco and six with PSG. The seasons he won with PSG are 2017-18, 2018-19, 2019-20, 2021-22, 2022-23, and 2023-24.
Mbappé is known for his incredible speed and technical skills on the field. In the 2018-19 season, he scored an amazing 33 goals, which earned him the Ligue 1 Player of the Year award. Not only has he been successful in club football, but he has also done well on the international stage.
Mbappé helped France win the 2018 FIFA World Cup, scoring four goals during the tournament, including one in the final match against Croatia. This performance made him one of the best young talents in the world.
5. Thiago Silva (7 titles)
Thiago Silva is a Brazilian footballer who is considered one of the best defenders in the world. He played as a center-back and was especially notable during his time at Paris Saint-Germain (PSG).
Silva joined PSG in 2012 from AC Milan, with the transfer fee reported to be around €42 million. During his eight years at PSG, Silva became a key player under coach Carlo Ancelotti and helped the team achieve great success.
One of Silva’s biggest achievements at PSG was winning the Ligue 1 title seven times. The only season PSG did not win the league during Silva’s time was in 2016-17, when AS Monaco finished first.
Silva’s leadership and defensive skills were crucial in helping PSG dominate French football during this period. Besides the Ligue 1 titles, Silva also won other trophies with PSG. These include six Coupes de la Ligue and five Coupes de France.
His time at PSG was capped by a historic run to the UEFA Champions League final in 2020. Although PSG did not win, losing to Bayern Munich, Silva became the first Brazilian to captain a team in a Champions League final.
After his successful career in France, Silva moved to Chelsea in the Premier League. At Chelsea, he continued to show his great talent, helping the team win the UEFA Champions League, FIFA Club World Cup, and UEFA Super Cup.
Silva played four seasons at Chelsea before deciding to return to his home country to join his first club, Fluminense, on a two-year contract.
His return to Fluminense marks the end of his time in Europe and allows him to finish his career in Brazil, where he began as a young player. Silva has had an incredible career and his contributions to PSG and Chelsea have made him a legend in the game.

6. Sidney Govou (7 titles)
Sidney Govou is one of the players who has won the most Ligue 1 titles, with seven championships to his name. Born on July 27, 1979, in Le Puy-en-Velay, France, Govou is a retired footballer who made a big impact during his career, especially at Olympique Lyonnais, where he spent most of his professional life.
He is best known for playing as a winger, using his speed and skill to help his team dominate French football during the 2000s. Govou joined Lyon’s youth academy in 1997 and worked his way up to the professional team, making his debut in 2000.
Over the next decade, he became a crucial player for Lyon. His time at the club was seen as an extraordinary period of success. From 2002 to 2008, Lyon won seven consecutive Ligue 1 titles, making them the top team in France during those years.
Govou played a key role in all of these victories, contributing with his speed, dribbling, and ability to create scoring chances. The seven titles he won with Lyon were in the 2001-02, 2002-03, 2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06, 2006-07, and 2007-08 seasons.
Govou also helped Lyon win the Coupe de la Ligue in 2001 and the Coupe de France in 2008. Govou wasn’t just successful at the club level. He also played for the French national team, earning 49 caps and scoring 10 goals from 2002 to 2010.
He was part of the squad that reached the final of the 2006 FIFA World Cup. However, After leaving Lyon in 2010, Govou played for other clubs, including Panathinaikos in Greece and Évian in France, before retiring.
7. Grégory Coupet (7 titles)
Grégory Coupet is an Incredible goalkeeper during his playing days. He was born on December 31, 1972, in Le Puy-en-Velay, France. Coupet started his football career with Club Olympique Le Puy as a young player.
He turned professional in 1994 with Saint-Étienne, where he made his debut in Ligue 1. In January 1997, Coupet made a surprising move to Olympique Lyonnais, leaving Saint-Étienne to replace the goalkeeper Pascal Olmeta.
This turned out to be a great decision, as Lyon soon became one of the most successful teams in Ligue 1. With Coupet as their goalkeeper, Lyon won seven consecutive Ligue 1 titles from 2002 to 2008.
This amazing achievement made Coupet one of the most successful players in the history of French football. Coupet was known for his incredible saves and strong presence in the goal.
One of his most memorable moments happened during a UEFA Champions League match against Barcelona in the 2001-02 season. In this game, Coupet first accidentally headed the ball towards his own goal but managed to save it by heading it onto the crossbar.
Just seconds later, he made an incredible save to stop a close-range header by Rivaldo. In the 2002-03 season, Coupet faced a tough time with Lyon due to a contract dispute. At one point, he even said he would never play for the club again.
However, the tragic death of his friend and former Lyon teammate Marc-Vivien Foé made him rethink his decision. Coupet eventually settled his differences with Lyon and continued to play for the team.
In 2005, he was voted into the top 10 for the IFFHS World’s Best Goalkeeper Award, finishing fourth. He was also named Ligue 1 Keeper of the Year in both 2004 and 2005.
Coupet’s time at Lyon ended in 2008 when he was sold to Atlético Madrid for €1.5 million. He later joined Paris Saint-Germain in 2009 and played there until he retired in 2011.
Throughout his career, Coupet won seven Ligue 1 titles, one Coupe de France, one Coupe de la Ligue, and five Trophée des Champions with Lyon.

Djamel Belmadi
(
Arabic
:
جَمَال بَلمَاضِيّ
; born 25 March 1976) is a professional
football
coach and former player. He is the current head coach of
Qatar Stars League
side
Al Duhail
. Born in France, he represented Algeria internationally between 2000 and 2004.
As a player he was
midfielder
who had spells in
Ligue 1
with
Paris Saint-Germain
,
Marseille
,
Cannes
and
Valenciennes
. He also briefly played in
La Liga
for
Celta Vigo
and in the
Premier League
for
Manchester City
. Later on in his career he returned to
England
and played several seasons at
Southampton
whilst the club were in the
Football League
. He also played for
Martigues
,
Al-Ittihad
and
Al-Kharitiyath
. Born in
France
, he played internationally for
Algeria
and was capped 20 times.
As a coach, Belmadi has managed
Lekhwiya
,
Qatar B
,
Qatar
,
Al-Duhail
[
a
]
and most recently, Algeria.
Club career
[
edit
]
France and Spain
[
edit
]
Born in
Champigny-sur-Marne
, France, Belmadi started his career at
Paris Saint-Germain
, making his debut in January 1996 against
Gueugnon
, before spending a season at
Martigues
. He spent the 1997–98 season at
Marseille
, and then moved to
Cannes
for the 1998–99 season. In August 1999, he was signed again by Marseille, but immediately went on loan to Spanish club
Celta Vigo
.
In January 2000, Belmadi returned to Marseille, eventually securing a regular place in the first team's midfield in 2000–01. In January 2001, he made good use of a rare opportunity presented him to play in Marseille's attack, when Liberian maestro
George Weah
—who had been the main attacker—was away on international duty with the Lone Stars of
Liberia
. Belmadi seized the opportunity to score a vital goal for Marseille against fellow strugglers
Toulouse
to keep Marseille just outside the relegation zone.
On 14 April 2001, he scored the winning goal in Marseille's 2–1 victory over
Sedan
, before a near–60,000 crowd, giving
Bernard Tapie
's team a much needed lifeline out of relegation.
Manchester City
[
edit
]
In January 2003, Belmadi had fallen out of favour at Marseille, now managed by
Alain Perrin
, who agreed to loan him to
Kevin Keegan
’s
Manchester City
after a successful trial. He joined ranks with fellow Algerian
Ali Benarbia
.
He made his full debut for Manchester City on 29 January 2003 at
Maine Road
in a 4–1 victory against
Fulham
(alongside another recruit from the French league –
David Sommeil
).
In Belmadi's brief time at Manchester City, he only made two starts and six substitute appearances, the last of which was in a  1–0 defeat against
Southampton
on 11 May 2003 in the final league game at Maine Road.
Although Kevin Keegan liked Belmadi's style of play, he conceded that he could not afford another free spirit in a side already containing
Eyal Berkovic
and Ali Bernabia, so Belmadi returned to Marseille.
In August 2003, he was released by Marseille and played the 2003–04 and 2004–05 seasons in
Qatar
with
Al-Ittihad
and
Al-Kharitiyath
.
Southampton
[
edit
]
In July 2005, after trials at
Celtic
,
Wigan Athletic
and
Sunderland
, Belmadi joined
Southampton
(then playing in the Football League Championship) for their pre-season tour of Scotland.
Harry Redknapp
initially gave Belmadi a one-month contract, and he made his debut on 6 August 2005 in a 0–0 draw against
Wolverhampton Wanderers
. His contract was extended until the end of the 2005–06 season after impressive performances in his early games, including a goal against
Crewe Alexandra
on 27 August 2005. In January 2006, he picked up a thigh injury, which put him out of the team until April.
Belmadi had, however, done enough to persuade Southampton, now managed by
George Burley
, to re-sign him for the 2006–07 season. This was again blighted by injury problems, including a knee injury picked up in September, which put him out until February. He picked up several other niggling injuries putting him out for long periods. When fit, there was no doubting Belmadi's ability and quality on the ball whether playing on the left or right of midfield. At his best, he could unpick defenses with his passing and kept the ball well. Unfortunately, his injuries restricted him to 40 appearances in his two years at
St Mary's
. His contract with the Saints expired on 30 June 2007 and was not renewed as Southampton faced up to the financial realities of a third season in
the Championship
.
[
2
]
Valenciennes
[
edit
]
After being released by Southampton, Belmadi returned to France and joined
Valenciennes
. He retired from football in 2009.
International career
[
edit
]
Belmadi made his debut for
Algeria
on 9 July 2000 against
Morocco
. He was part of the Algerian
2004 African Nations Cup
team, who finished second in their group in the first round of competition before being defeated by Morocco in the quarter-finals. Belmadi last played for Algeria in a World Cup qualifier against
Zimbabwe
on 20 June 2004, having made 20 appearances and scoring 5 goals.
Managerial career
[
edit
]
Lekhwiya
[
edit
]
Belmadi coaching Lekhwiya in a
Qatar Stars League
match against
Al Sadd
In the summer of 2010, Belmadi was appointed as the head coach of newly promoted
Qatar Stars League
club
Lekhwiya
.
[
3
]
In his first season with the club, he led them to the
2010–11 Qatar Stars League
title for the first time in the club's history. He also led them to the final of the
2010 Sheikh Jassem Cup
, where they lost to
Al Arabi
.
For the second time,
Lekhwiya
won the
2011–12 Qatar Stars League
title, under the management of Belmadi. He resigned on 8 October 2012 after a bad start of the 2012–13 season.
Qatar B
[
edit
]
In December 2013, Belmadi was appointed as head coach of the
Qatar B
team, which was set to participate in the
2014 WAFF Championship
on home soil. He called up a number of foreigners to the national team, including compatriots
Boualem Khoukhi
and
Karim Boudiaf
after being informed by the
QFA
that they were eligible to compete for Qatar.
[
4
]
Qatar were crowned champions of the 2014 WAFF Championship after defeating
Jordan
on 7 January.
[
5
]
They finished the tournament undefeated, with 10 goals scored and a single goal conceded.
Qatar senior team
[
edit
]
On 15 March 2014, Belmadi was unveiled as the new head coach of the
Qatar senior football team
, replacing
Fahad Thani
.
[
6
]
His first match as Qatar coach was a 0–0 draw with
Macedonia
. He led his team to a notable 1–0 first-ever victory over
Australia
in a friendly match on 14 October 2014, after having posted a 5–0 win over
Lebanon
and a 3–0 victory over
Uzbekistan
in their two previous matches.
[
7
]
In correspondence to Qatar's performance in the aforementioned friendly matches, sports channel
Al Kass
stated that Qatar is "showing signs of evolution with Belmadi" and that the team was "undergoing a renewal."
[
8
]
He led Qatar to win the
22nd Arabian Gulf Cup
by beating host
Saudi Arabia
in the final. However, Qatar showed a poor form in the
2015 AFC Asian Cup
and was eliminated in the group stages after three consecutive defeats by
United Arab Emirates
,
Iran
and
Bahrain
. He was dismissed from his post on 30 April 2015.
[
9
]
Al-Duhail
[
edit
]
On 19 June 2015, Belmadi was appointed for the second time in his career to coach
Lekhwiya
; he was a replacement for
Michael Laudrup
. In 2017, the club was rebranded to Al-Duhail SC following the absorption of
El Jaish
.
[
citation needed
]
Algeria
[
edit
]
On 2 August 2018, Belmadi became the manager of the
Algeria national team
.
[
10
]
At his second international football championship (having coached Qatar in the
2015 AFC Asian Cup
), Belmadi's Algerian team was not considered a serious contender for the trophy because Algeria's performance in the
2019 Africa Cup of Nations qualification
was not promising, despite topping the group with two draws to
Gambia
and an away-loss to
Benin
. The unimpressive qualification campaign increased the pressure on Belmadi.
Despite heavy criticism, Belmadi led Algeria to success and earned his first international trophy. Algeria defeated every opponent on its road to the final of the
2019 Africa Cup of Nations
(AFCON) held in Egypt, including two victories over
Senegal
in the group stage and the
final
. Algeria won its second continental title and became the North African second team, after
Egypt
, to win more than one AFCON trophy.
[
11
]
In the
2021 AFCON
, the defending champions Algeria finished last in their group to be eliminated from the tournament.
[
12
]
During the
2022 World Cup qualification
third round, Algeria failed to qualify to the final tournament in Qatar, having lost on away goals rule against
Cameroon
following a 2–2 draw on aggregate.
[
13
]
In January 2023, Belmadi extended his contract until 2026.
[
14
]
In the
2023 AFCON
held in
Ivory Coast
, Algeria led by Belmadi exited the tournament after their defeat against
Mauritania
, without scoring any win in the group phase.
[
15
]
On 24 January 2024, Belmadi's position as national team manager was terminated by mutual consent.
[
16
]
However, despite immediately resigning himself in front of the players, Belmadi asked the
FAF
for a severance package worth 29 months of salary, equivalent to €7 million. Faced with a refusal from the FAF, he then threatened to bring the matter to the FIFA for a ruling.
[
17
]
Return to Al-Duhail
[
edit
]
In June 2025, Belmadi returned to Al-Duhail for his third spell as head coach.
[
18
]
Bank theft incident
[
edit
]
While Belmadi was with Manchester City, he, along with players
Daniel Van Buyten
and
Vicente Vuoso
, were the victims of a theft by two bank workers. At the time that Belmadi left Manchester City, he left £230,000 in an account with the
Co-operative Bank
. In total, the bank workers stole more than £350,000 from the accounts of the three players.
In January 2006, the bank workers, Paul Sherwood, a cashier, and Paul Hanley, his supervisor, were jailed for 32 months and 12 months respectively.
